title: Morning Rush at the Espresso Bar
briefing: You are opening barista on a busy morning. Grind fresh beans, pull an espresso and hand it off at the pickup counter.

lines.intro: Morning! Grind the beans, pull a shot, mark it with milk and get it to the pickup counter.
One macchiato, please. I'm running late!

objectives.label: Take Leo's order
objectives.tip: Repeat the order back so nothing gets lost between register and bar.

objectives.label: Check in with Maya
objectives.tip: Check the queue with your lead before you start, so you know what is coming.

objectives.label: Grab the bag of beans
objectives.tip: Fresh beans, used within a few weeks of roasting, give the best flavour.

objectives.label: Load the beans into the grinder
objectives.tip: Fill the hopper part way so the beans stay fresh.

objectives.label: Grind the beans

say.text: Smell that? Fresh grounds for every shot.

objectives.tip: Grind just before brewing, about as fine as table salt for espresso.

objectives.label: Grab a cup for Leo's order
objectives.tip: A warm cup keeps the espresso hot, so take one from the cup warmer.

objectives.label: Pass the cup to the bar
objectives.tip: Line cups up in order on the hand-off so the bar makes drinks first come, first served.

objectives.label: Grab the milk jug
objectives.tip: Use cold milk straight from the fridge. It steams smoother and gives you more time.

objectives.label: Set the jug on the steamer
objectives.tip: Fill the jug only to the bottom of the spout so the milk has room to stretch.

objectives.label: Steam milk for the next order
objectives.tip: Stop at about 60-65 C, too hot to hold the jug for long. Hotter scalds the milk.

objectives.label: Take the cup from the hand-off
objectives.tip: Check the order on the cup before you start the shot.

objectives.label: Seat the cup under the main machine
objectives.tip: Centre the cup under both spouts so the shot pours evenly.

objectives.label: Pull the espresso shot

say.text: Nice crema. About 25 seconds is right.

objectives.tip: Aim for 25 to 30 seconds. Fast shots taste sour, slow ones bitter.

objectives.label: Grab the steamed milk
objectives.tip: Swirl the jug so the foam and milk stay together.
objectives.real: Baristas finish milk drinks right away, before the foam separates.

objectives.label: Mark the shot with milk
objectives.tip: Just a spoonful of foam on top. That is what makes it a macchiato.
objectives.real: Pouring is the craft customers see: the right amount of milk is the whole drink.

objectives.label: Take the espresso
objectives.tip: Serve it within a minute, before the crema fades.

objectives.label: Set the espresso on the pickup counter
objectives.tip: Set it down with the handle turned toward the customer.

objectives.label: Ring the bell for Leo
objectives.tip: Call the drink and the name clearly so the right person takes it.

announce.text: The main machine's group head just clogged! Grab the spare cup and use the backup machine.

replaceRemaining.label: Grab the spare cup
replaceRemaining.tip: In a rush you switch machines and keep the line moving.

replaceRemaining.label: Seat the cup under the backup machine
replaceRemaining.tip: Flush the backup group head first to clear out old coffee.

replaceRemaining.label: Pull the shot on the backup

say.text: Good save. That's how a rush goes.

replaceRemaining.tip: Watch the time again. Every machine pulls a little differently.

replaceRemaining.label: Grab the steamed milk
replaceRemaining.tip: Swirl the jug so the foam and milk stay together.
replaceRemaining.real: Baristas finish milk drinks right away, before the foam separates.

replaceRemaining.label: Mark the shot with milk
replaceRemaining.tip: Just a spoonful of foam on top. That is what makes it a macchiato.
replaceRemaining.real: Pouring is the craft customers see: the right amount of milk is the whole drink.

replaceRemaining.label: Take the espresso
replaceRemaining.tip: Check the crema. A good shot has a thick golden layer.

replaceRemaining.label: Set the espresso on the pickup counter
replaceRemaining.tip: Set it down with the handle turned toward the customer.

replaceRemaining.label: Ring the bell for Leo
replaceRemaining.tip: Apologise briefly for the wait. Regulars remember how you handle it.

facts: A standard espresso shot takes about 25 to 30 seconds to pull.
Baristas adjust the grind size through the day as humidity changes.
Espresso is brewed at around 9 bar of pressure.
Coffee beans start losing aroma within minutes of grinding.

order.waiting: Is my macchiato nearly ready? I have a train.

career.dayInLife: Open before sunrise: dial in the grinder, prep milk and pastries, then serve a steady line. Between rushes you clean, restock and chat with regulars. Close with a deep clean of the machines.
career.schedule: Early mornings, weekends and holidays, 4 to 8 hour shifts.

physical.note: On your feet all shift with repetitive wrist work.

people.note: Constant customer contact and quick teamwork.

pressure.note: Morning rushes stack orders, and speed and accuracy both count.

loves: Regulars who know you by name
The craft of dialing in a great shot
hard: Very early starts and weekend work
Sore feet and wrists by the end of a shift
Staying friendly with rude customers mid-rush
career.start: No degree needed. Most baristas learn on the job in a few weeks. Specialty cafes value courses such as the SCA Barista Foundation.

roles.label: Register
roles.brief: Take the order, start the cup, prep milk, and call it out when it is ready.

roles.label: Bar
roles.brief: Grind, pull the shot and get it to the pickup counter.
